title: Week 26 Reading Quiz
description_html: Read both lessons before you start. Choose the best answer for each question. You may take this quiz twice, and your higher score counts.

questions.name: Question 1
questions.text_html: When Texas joined the Confederacy, the army left the frontier forts and most Texas fighting men went east. What was one result?

answers.text: Comanche and Kiowa raiders gained a few years of strength they had not had in a decade.
The Comanche signed a treaty with Texas and ended all of their raids while the army was gone.
The frontier line moved steadily farther west as settlers pushed ahead.
The bison herds grew larger across the southern plains during the war.

questions.name: Question 2
questions.text_html: The Quahadi did not sign the Medicine Lodge treaty of 1867. What does this fact help explain?

answers.text: Why the Army never fought the Quahadi at any time in the Red River War or in the years after.
Why Quanah Parker never took part in any war party or battle.
Why bison hunters left Texas before the great herds were gone in the 1870s.
Why some Comanche stayed free on the Llano Estacado after others agreed to a reservation.

questions.name: Question 3
questions.text_html: The army was glad when hunters killed the southern bison herds. What does that tell you about its strategy?

answers.text: The army wanted to feed its soldiers on bison meat during the winter.
The army wanted the hunters kept safe from raiding parties on the plains.
Without bison, the Plains peoples could no longer live as they had.
The army wanted the hides to make new coats and uniforms for its men.

questions.name: Question 4
questions.text_html: Mackenzie's men captured about 1,400 horses at Palo Duro Canyon and shot most of them. Why was this so damaging?

answers.text: Horses were the only food that the Comanche had, and the army wanted to starve them out.
The horses had belonged to Texan ranchers.
The Rangers had asked for the horses to be destroyed.
Without horses, a Plains people could not hunt or move camp.

questions.name: Question 5
questions.text_html: The lesson says that in the Red River War the main force against the Comanche was the U.S. Army, though the Rangers took part. Which detail supports this?

answers.text: The Rangers fought at Palo Duro Canyon without any help from the army.
The Army never entered Texas at any point during the Red River War.
The Army marched from several directions under officers such as Mackenzie.
The Frontier Battalion was created only after the war had come to an end.

questions.name: Question 6
questions.text_html: After 1875, the Rangers' Frontier Battalion hunted outlaws such as Sam Bass instead of raiders. What does this show?

answers.text: The Rangers were disbanded by the legislature after the Comanche were beaten.
The Rangers' work turned toward law enforcement once the raiding frontier closed.
The Comanche had become outlaws themselves and were hunted as criminals.
The Rangers had left Texas for good and moved north into Kansas.

questions.name: Question 7
questions.text_html: The windmill spread across the plains in the 1880s. Why did it matter for ranching on the Llano Estacado?

answers.text: It kept the bison herds away from the cattle on the open grass, so that more grass was left.
It cut the cost of barbed wire for every rancher on the plains.
It took the place of the railroads for hauling cattle across the plains.
It pumped water from underground, so ranchers no longer had to stay near a river.
